nba:401909891.headline: Unbeaten Thunder arrive in Dallas with half a rotation on the shelf
nba:401909891.read: Oklahoma City is 4-0 with a plus-10.5 margin and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander at 27.2 a night, but the injury report is the story: Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace and Alex Caruso are all out, Williams and Wallace for surgery, and Ajay Mitchell is questionable. Dallas is 2-2 and getting outscored by 3.5 per game, though Cooper Flagg at 25 points, 6.3 assists and 3.7 steals gives them the second-best player on the floor, with Kyrie Irving questionable and Dereck Lively out. The model has OKC at 79 percent, which feels like a rating built on the full roster; with that many starters missing and Dallas at home, this is much closer to a coin flip. Four games in, nobody's margin means much yet.
keys: OKC missing Holmgren, J. Williams, Wallace, Caruso

nba:401909881.headline: Winless Heat get a Hawks team that scores 121 a night
nba:401909881.read: Miami is 0-4 and giving up 121.8 points per game, a minus-12.8 margin that is the worst in this slate, even with Giannis Antetokounmpo producing 28.5 and 9.5. Atlanta is 2-2 but its plus-9.2 margin says the losses were close and the wins were not, and Jalen Johnson is filling the sheet at 21.5, 9.8 and 8.2. The Hawks have dropped two straight and are 0-1 at home, so this is not a lock, but the gap in how the two teams have played is wide. Both teams are rested.

nba:401909882.headline: Cavs 2-0 at home, but the margins say this is tighter than the model thinks
nba:401909882.read: Cleveland is 2-1 and unbeaten at home with Donovan Mitchell at 26.7 a game and a clean injury report, which is rare this time of year. The catch is a minus-0.7 margin, so the Cavs have been winning close and losing comfortably. Washington is 2-2 with an almost even margin behind Anthony Davis at 22.8 and 9.2 and Trae Young handing out 11 assists, though AJ Dybantsa is listed out. The model's 82 percent for Cleveland is steeper than the numbers support; call it closer to two in three.

nba:401909883.headline: Short-handed Hornets catch the Pistons on a back-to-back
nba:401909883.read: Detroit is 3-1 with a plus-6 margin and Cade Cunningham running things at 20.8 points and 8 assists, but it played last night, Jalen Duren is out two weeks with a hamstring, and Isaiah Joe is day to day. Charlotte is also 3-1, but with a minus-7 margin, and it is missing Coby White, Kon Knueppel and Grant Williams, leaning on Brandon Miller at 24.2 and Naz Reid inside. The rest edge belongs to Charlotte and the talent edge belongs to Detroit; the Pistons' margin is the more honest number of the two 3-1 records.
keys: Detroit on second night of back-to-back

nba:401909884.headline: Pacers' banged-up backcourt tilts this toward Maxey and Philly
nba:401909884.read: Indiana has Tyrese Haliburton and Andrew Nembhard both questionable, T.J. McConnell and Ivica Zubac out, and Ben Sheppard and Johnny Furphy lost for long stretches, which is a lot of guard minutes and rim protection missing from a 2-2 team that was only plus-1.5 to begin with. Philadelphia is 3-1 at plus-3 with Tyrese Maxey at 28.8 a night, Joel Embiid at 9.7 boards and LeBron James leading the team in assists; its absences are deeper bench pieces. The model has Philly at 64 percent and that reads right, with the number climbing if Haliburton sits.
keys: Haliburton questionable, McConnell and Zubac out
Both teams coming off a loss

nba:401909885.headline: Magic without Banchero and Suggs visit a Raptors team that's been winning big
nba:401909885.read: Orlando is 1-2 and minus-6.6 with Paolo Banchero out four to six weeks, Jalen Suggs out two weeks and Jonathan Isaac ruled out, leaving Franz Wagner to carry it at 21 points, 8.3 boards and 6.3 assists. Toronto is 2-1 with a plus-10 margin, 1-0 at home, and spreading it around behind RJ Barrett at 21; it is missing Brandon Ingram and Kawhi Leonard for weeks, so neither side is whole. The Raptors have simply been the better team with what they have, and Orlando's offense at 109.7 a game is the problem that doesn't fix itself tonight.
keys: Ingram and Leonard out for Raptors

nba:401909886.headline: Tired Knicks still the pick against a Bulls defense giving up 129
nba:401909886.read: Chicago is 1-3 with a minus-18.7 margin and is allowing 129.5 points per game, numbers that are hard to overstate even in a four-game sample, and Nic Claxton is still out while Patrick Williams and Tobe Awaka are questionable. New York is 1-3 too, but at minus-1.3 with Karl-Anthony Towns pulling 14 rebounds a night and Jalen Brunson at 22.8. The Knicks won last night in Detroit and are on a back-to-back, which is the one reason to pause, and Jose Alvarado's status is unclear. The model's 59 percent for New York is fair; the rest disadvantage keeps this from being higher.

nba:401909887.headline: Rockets go for 5-0 with no Sengun and no Adams in the middle
nba:401909887.read: Houston is 4-0 with a plus-9.8 margin and Kevin Durant leading the way at 23.5, but Alperen Sengun is out with a back issue, Steven Adams is sidelined a week or two, and Marcus Smart is questionable, so the frontcourt depth that fueled this start is thin tonight. Milwaukee is 1-3 and minus-5.5 but has a clean injury report and Tyler Herro at 23.5 points and 5.8 assists, and it took its one win at home. The model gives Houston 80 percent; with both centers out I would shade that down toward 70, but the Rockets are still the clearly better team on paper and on the court so far.
keys: Sengun and Adams out for Houston

nba:401909888.headline: Wolves have been blowing teams out, even with Edwards now out two months
nba:401909888.read: Minnesota is 3-1 with a plus-17 margin, scoring 122 and allowing 105, and Rudy Gobert is averaging 14.2 boards. The big caveat is Anthony Edwards, who will have knee surgery and miss up to two months, and Donte DiVincenzo remains out, so the scoring load shifts to Jaden McDaniels and LaMelo Ball. Golden State is 1-3 and minus-3.5, with Stephen Curry at 23.7 but Yaxel Lendeborg, its best all-around producer at 21.8 and 9.2, questionable, and Jimmy Butler, Kristaps Porzingis and Moses Moody all out long term. The Warriors are thinner than the Wolves even after Edwards' news, and Minnesota is at home.
keys: Edwards out up to two months
Lendeborg questionable, Butler and Porzingis out

nba:401909889.headline: Jokic against a winless but high-scoring Pelicans team
nba:401909889.read: Neither defense has shown up: Denver is 1-2 and allowing 121.7 a night for a minus-8.7 margin, and New Orleans is 0-3 but scoring 124.7 and only minus-3.3. Nikola Jokic is doing his usual 22.3, 9.7 and 8.7, while the Pelicans have balance with Zion Williamson at 20.7 and Dejounte Murray at 20.3 with 2.3 steals. Denver is down Cameron Johnson, who is doubtful, plus Julian Strawther and Alpha Diallo, while New Orleans is missing Yves Missi inside. The model leans Denver at 59 percent and I lean the same way because of Jokic, but Denver's margin is actually the worse of the two, so it is a thin edge.

nba:401909890.headline: Spurs on a back-to-back, but Utah's injury list runs deeper
nba:401909890.read: San Antonio is 2-2 at plus-6.7 and has won two straight, with Victor Wembanyama at 22.2 points, 10.8 rebounds and 4.2 blocks and De'Aaron Fox at 7.8 assists. The Spurs played last night and Tobias Harris' availability is unclear after a calf issue, which is the case for Utah. The Jazz are 1-3 and minus-8.2 with Jaren Jackson Jr. out six to eight weeks and Jusuf Nurkic out at least a month, and Lauri Markkanen is questionable with a wrist. Keyonte George is producing at 22.8 and 7.8 assists, but if Markkanen sits the Jazz have very little to throw at Wembanyama. The model's 73 percent for the Spurs looks about right.
keys: Spurs on second night of back-to-back
Jackson Jr. and Nurkic out, Markkanen questionable

nba:401909892.headline: Doncic's 36 a night against rested Clippers who are short on wings
nba:401909892.read: The Lakers are 3-1 with a plus-8 margin, scoring 128.3 per game with Luka Doncic at 36 points and 8.2 assists, but they lost last night and are on a back-to-back heading into the Clippers' building. The Clippers are rested at 1-2 with a plus-3.3 margin and Darius Garland at 24 and 7, though Rui Hachimura has been ruled out and Bradley Beal and Max Strus are still sidelined. The model has the Clippers at 58 percent, presumably on the rest and home edge, and that is a reasonable position. I lean the other way because Los Angeles has been the better team by five points of margin and the Clippers are thin at forward, but this is close.
keys: Hachimura out, Beal and Strus out
